This is a reverse-engineering benchmark. You are given a compiled binary and its documentation.
Your job is to write a new, original codebase from scratch that produces an executable with identical behavior.
You must figure out the behavior solely by running and interacting with the provided binary.
Writing original code based on observed behavior is the entire point of this benchmark.

Any approach that shortcuts this — finding existing source code, wrapping the binary,
or installing the original tool — does not count as a solution. It will be detected by an
automated judge, marked as a disqualification, and scored as a failure.
The trace will be posted to an online wall of shame.

<RULES>
## What is not allowed

### 1. Obtaining source code

The only source of truth about what the executable does is the executable itself and its
bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Cloning or browsing the original GitHub repository, its forks, or mirrors
- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.
- Fetching source tarballs from project websites (e.g., `curl https://lua.org/ftp/lua-5.5.0.tar.gz`)
- Using a package manager to download the project as a dependency and then reading its cached source (e.g., navigating into `~/.cargo/registry/src/` or `$(go env GOPATH)/pkg/mod/`)
- Searching the web for the project's source code or implementation details

### 2. Wrapping or reusing the original binary

Your submission must be a genuine reimplementation. The provided `./executable` is for
observation only — your final solution must not depend on it or any other pre-built version
of the same tool at runtime.

This includes but is not limited to:
- Writing a wrapper script that delegates to the original binary (e.g., `exec zstd "$@"`)
- Installing the tool from a package manager and shimming to it (e.g., `apt-get install nnn && cp $(which nnn) ./executable`)
- Writing a `compile.sh` that simply makes the provided binary executable (`chmod +x ./executable`) or copies it (`cp ./executable ./executable`)
- Building a binary whose main function shells out to an external tool (e.g., `Command::new("miniserve").args(args).exec()`)
- Re-linking prebuilt `.o` object files found in the workspace without writing new source code

### 3. Binary analysis of the provided executable

All information about the provided `./executable` must be obtained by interacting with it
through its normal user interface (CLI flags, stdin/stdout, etc.).
- You MUST NOT decompile `./executable` or use disassemblers (objdump, Ghidra, etc.) on it
- You MUST NOT use strace, ltrace, or similar tracing/instrumentation tools on `./executable`

Note: this restriction applies ONLY to the provided `./executable`. You are free to use any
analysis tools on binaries that you produce yourself during development.

## What IS allowed

- Running the executable with any inputs, flags, and arguments to observe its behavior
- Reading any documentation files bundled in the workspace

# go-critic

Highly extensible Go source code linter providing checks currently missing from other linters.

![Logo](https://avatars1.githubusercontent.com/u/40007520?s=300&u=b44287d8845a63fb0102d5259710c11ea367bb13&v=4)

## Description

go-critic is a Go source code linter that provides almost 100 diagnostics checking for bugs, performance issues, and style problems. It includes opinionated checks with strict requirements and supports extensibility through dynamic rules.

## Features

* Almost 100 diagnostics that check for bugs, performance and style issues
* Extensible without re-compilation with dynamic rules
* Includes `#opinionated` checks with very strict and specific requirements
* Self-documented: `go-critic doc <checkname>` gives a checker description

## Installation

For most users, using `go-critic` under [golangci-lint](https://github.com/golangci/golangci-lint) is enough.

Precompiled `go-critic` binaries can be found at [releases](https://github.com/go-critic/go-critic/releases) page.

It can be installed in the usual Go way by running:

```bash
go install -v github.com/go-critic/go-critic/cmd/go-critic@latest
```

On macOS, you can also install `go-critic` using either Homebrew or MacPorts:

[Homebrew](https://brew.sh)

```zsh
brew install go-critic
```

[MacPorts](https://www.macports.org)

```zsh
sudo port install go-critic
```

## Usage

Be sure `go-critic` executable is under your `$PATH`.

Usage of **go-critic**: `go-critic [sub-command] [sub-command args...]`
Run `go-critic` without arguments to get help output.

```
Supported sub-commands:
	check - run linter over specified targets
		$ go-critic check -help
		$ go-critic check -v -enable='paramTypeCombine,unslice' strings bytes
		$ go-critic check -v -enable='#diagnostic' -disable='#experimental,#opinionated' ./...
	version - print linter version
		$ go-critic version
	doc - get installed checkers documentation
		$ go-critic doc -help
		$ go-critic doc
		$ go-critic doc checkerName
```

### Examples

```bash
# Runs all stable checkers on `fmt` package:
go-critic check fmt

# Run all stable checkers on `pkg1` and `pkg2`
go-critic check pkg1 pkg2

# Run all stable checkers on `fmt` package and configure rangeExprCopy checker
go-critic check -@rangeExprCopy.sizeThreshold 128 fmt

# Runs specified checkers on `fmt` package:
go-critic check -enable elseif,paramName fmt

# Run all stable checkers on current dir and all its children recursively:
go-critic check ./...

# Like above, but without `appendAssign` check:
go-critic check -disable=appendAssign ./...

# Run all stable checkers on `foo.go` file:
go-critic check foo.go

# Run stable diagnostics over `strings` package:
go-critic check -enable='#diagnostic' -disable='#experimental' strings

# Run all stable and non-opinionated checks:
go-critic check -enableAll -disable='#experimental,#opinionated' ./src/...
```

> To get a list of available checker parameters, run `go-critic doc <checkerName>`.

### Checker Tags

In place of a single name, **tag** can be used. Tag is a named checkers group.

Tags:

* `#diagnostic` - kind of checks that detect various errors in code
* `#style` - kind of checks that find style issues in code
* `#performance` - kind of checks that detect potential performance issues in code
* `#experimental` - check is under testing and development. Disabled by default
* `#opinionated` - check can be unwanted for some people. Disabled by default
* `#security` - kind of checks that find security issues in code. Disabled by default

## Documentation

For complete documentation and a full list of checkers, visit [go-critic.com](https://go-critic.com/overview).

### dupArg
Detects suspicious duplicated arguments.

Non-compliant code:
copy(dst, dst)

Compliant code:
copy(dst, src)

### dupBranchBody
Detects duplicated branch bodies inside conditional statements.

Non-compliant code:
if cond {
	println("cond=true")
} else {
	println("cond=true")
}

Compliant code:
if cond {
	println("cond=true")
} else {
	println("cond=false")
}

### dupCase
Detects duplicated case clauses inside switch or select statements.

Non-compliant code:
switch x {
case ys[0], ys[1], ys[2], ys[0], ys[4]:
}

Compliant code:
switch x {
case ys[0], ys[1], ys[2], ys[3], ys[4]:
}

### dupImport
Detects multiple imports of the same package under different aliases.

Non-compliant code:
import (
	"fmt"
	printing "fmt" // Imported the second time
)

Compliant code:
import(
	"fmt"
)

### dupOption
Detects duplicated option function arguments in variadic function calls.

Non-compliant code:
doSomething(name,
		withWidth(w),
		withHeight(h),
		withWidth(w),
)

Compliant code:
doSomething(name,
		withWidth(w),
		withHeight(h),
)

### dupSubExpr
Detects suspicious duplicated sub-expressions.

Non-compliant code:
sort.Slice(xs, func(i, j int) bool {
	return xs[i].v < xs[i].v // Duplicated index
})

Compliant code:
sort.Slice(xs, func(i, j int) bool {
	return xs[i].v < xs[j].v
})

### dynamicFmtString
Detects suspicious formatting strings usage.

Non-compliant code:

Compliant code:
errors.New(msg) or fmt.Errorf("%s", msg)

### elseif
Detects else with nested if statement that can be replaced with else-if.

Non-compliant code:

} else {
	if x := cond2; x {
	}
}

Compliant code:
if cond1 {
} else if x := cond2; x {
}

Checker parameters:

    	whether to skip balanced if-else pairs (default true)

### emptyDecl
Detects suspicious empty declarations blocks.

Compliant code:
/* nothing */

Detects fallthrough that can be avoided by using multi case values.

case reflect.Int32:
	return Int
}

Compliant code:
switch kind {
case reflect.Int, reflect.Int32:
	return Int
}

### emptyStringTest
Detects empty string checks that can be written more idiomatically.

Compliant code:
s == ""

### equalFold
Detects unoptimal strings/bytes case-insensitive comparison.

Non-compliant code:
strings.ToLower(x) == strings.ToLower(y)

Compliant code:
strings.EqualFold(x, y)

### evalOrder
Detects unwanted dependencies on the evaluation order.

Non-compliant code:

Compliant code:
err := f(&x)
return x, err

### exitAfterDefer
Detects calls to exit/fatal inside functions that use defer.

Non-compliant code:
defer os.Remove(filename)
if bad {
	log.Fatalf("something bad happened")
}

Compliant code:
defer os.Remove(filename)
if bad {
	log.Printf("something bad happened")
	return
}

### exposedSyncMutex
Detects exposed methods from sync.Mutex and sync.RWMutex.

Non-compliant code:
type Foo struct{ ...; sync.Mutex; ... }

Compliant code:
type Foo struct{ ...; mu sync.Mutex; ... }

### externalErrorReassign
Detects suspicious reassignment of error from another package.

Non-compliant code:
io.EOF = nil

Compliant code:
/* don't do it */

### filepathJoin
Detects problems in filepath.Join() function calls.

Non-compliant code:

Compliant code:
filepath.Join("dir", filename)

### flagDeref
Detects immediate dereferencing of `flag` package pointers.

Compliant code:

Detects suspicious flag names.

Compliant code:

https://github.com/golang/go/issues/41792

### hexLiteral
Detects hex literals that have mixed case letter digits.

Non-compliant code:

y := 0xfF

Compliant code:

// (A)

### httpNoBody
Detects nil usages in http.NewRequest calls, suggesting http.NoBody as an alternative.

Non-compliant code:

Compliant code:

Detects params that incur excessive amount of copying.

### ifElseChain
Detects repeated if-else statements and suggests to replace them with switch statement.

Non-compliant code:
if cond1 {
	// Code A.
} else if cond2 {
	// Code B.
} else {
	// Code C.
}

Compliant code:
switch {
case cond1:
	// Code A.
case cond2:
	// Code B.
default:
	// Code C.
}

Permits single else or else-if; repeated else-if or else + else-if
will trigger suggestion to use switch statement.
See [EffectiveGo#switch](https://golang.org/doc/effective_go.html#switch).

Checker parameters:
  -@ifElseChain.minThreshold int
    	min number of if-else blocks that makes the warning trigger (default 2)

Detects when imported package names shadowed in the assignments.

Compliant code:
filename := "foo.txt"

### indexAlloc
Detects strings.Index calls that may cause unwanted allocs.

Non-compliant code:

Compliant code:
bytes.Index(x, []byte(y))

See Go issue for details: https://github.com/golang/go/issues/25864

### initClause
Detects non-assignment statements inside if/switch init clause.

Non-compliant code:
if sideEffect(); cond {
}

Compliant code:
sideEffect()
if cond {
}

### mapKey
Detects suspicious map literal keys.

Non-compliant code:
_ = map[string]int{
	"foo": 1,
	"bar ": 2,
}

Compliant code:
_ = map[string]int{
	"foo": 1,
	"bar": 2,
}

### methodExprCall
Detects method expression call that can be replaced with a method call.

Non-compliant code:
f := foo{}
foo.bar(f)

Compliant code:
f := foo{}
f.bar()

### nestingReduce
Finds where nesting level could be reduced.

Non-compliant code:
for _, v := range a {
	if v.Bool {
		body()
	}
}

Compliant code:
for _, v := range a {
	if !v.Bool {
		continue
	}
	body()
}

Checker parameters:
  -@nestingReduce.bodyWidth int
    	min number of statements inside a branch to trigger a warning (default 5)

### newDeref
Detects immediate dereferencing of `new` expressions.

Non-compliant code:
x := *new(bool)

Compliant code:
x := false

### nilValReturn
Detects return statements those results evaluate to nil.

Non-compliant code:
if err == nil {
	return err
}

Compliant code:

if err == nil {
	return nil
}
// (B) - typo in "==", change to "!="
if err != nil {
	return err
}

### octalLiteral
Detects old-style octal literals.

Non-compliant code:
foo(02)

Compliant code:
foo(0o2)

### offBy1
Detects various off-by-one kind of errors.

Non-compliant code:
xs[len(xs)]

Compliant code:
xs[len(xs)-1]

Detects if function parameters could be combined by type and suggest the way to do it.

Non-compliant code:

Compliant code:

        self.assertEqual((p.returncode, p.stdout, p.stderr),

        p = self.run_command("help")
        self.assertTrue(p.stdout.startswith("Usage:\n\n    go-critic <command>"))
        self.assertEqual(p.stderr, "")
        p = self.run_command("doc", "appendAssign")
        self.assertIn("Detects suspicious append result assignments.", p.stdout)
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode, 0)
        p = self.run_command("doc", "noSuchChecker")
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode, 1)
        self.assertEqual(p.stderr, 'checker with name "noSuchChecker" not found\n')
        self.assertEqual(self.run_command("").stderr, "")

    def test_order_and_locations(self):
        self.write("input.go", "package demo\nfunc f(x int) {\n x = x + 1\n _ = x == x\n}\n")
        p = self.run_command("check", "input.go")
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode, 1)
        self.assertEqual(p.stdout, "")
        self.assertEqual(p.stderr,
            "./input.go:3:2: assignOp: replace `x = x + 1` with `x++`\n"
            "./input.go:4:6: dupSubExpr: suspicious identical LHS and RHS for `==` operator\n")
        p = self.run_command("check", "-enable=dupSubExpr", "-exitCode=7", "input.go")
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode, 7)
        self.assertNotIn("assignOp", p.stderr)
        p = self.run_command("check", "-enable=assignOp", "-shorterErrLocation=false", "input.go")
        self.assertTrue(p.stderr.startswith(str(self.root / "input.go") + ":3:2:"))

    def test_selection_and_flag_errors(self):
        p = self.run_command("check", "-enable=notARealChecker")
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode, 1)
        self.assertEqual(p.stderr, "init checkers: empty checkers set selected\n")
        p = self.run_command("check", "-help")
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode, 1)
        self.assertTrue(p.stderr.startswith("Usage of go-critic:\n"))
        self.assertTrue(p.stderr.endswith("parse args: flag: help requested\n"))
        p = self.run_command("doc", "-help")
        self.assertEqual((p.returncode, p.stderr),
                         (0, "Usage of go-critic:\nflag: help requested\n"))

    def test_generated_and_test_files(self):
        self.write("go.mod", "module example.com/demo\n\ngo 1.21\n")
        self.write("input.go", "package demo\nfunc f(x int) { x=x+1 }\n")
        self.write("input_test.go", "package demo\nfunc g(x int) { x=x+2 }\n")
        p = self.run_command("check", "-enable=assignOp", ".")
        self.assertEqual(p.returncode, 1)
        self.assertIn("input.go:", p.stderr)
        self.assertIn("input_test.go:", p.stderr)
        p = self.run_command("check", "-enable=assignOp", "-checkTests=false", ".")
        self.assertNotIn("input_test.go:", p.stderr)

        self.assertIn("hugeParam: xs is heavy (1024 bytes)", p.stderr)
        self.assertIn("rangeExprCopy: copy of xs (1024 bytes) can be avoided with &xs", p.stderr)


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
